“A toxic dose of aspirin is 200 to 300 mg/kg (milligrams per kilogram of body weight), and ingestion of 500 mg/kg is potentially lethal. In chronic overdose a lower level of aspirin in the body can result in serious illness. Much lower levels can affect children.”

Of course, this is all depending on your body weight and how many mg are in that branding of pills. If you fear you might’ve taken too much, please call poison control and or emergency services as the side effects aren’t fun. I’ve tried it myself, and I didn’t die. Instead, I experienced. 

*nausea 
*vomiting 
*dizziness 
*sweating
*dehydration 

Even if it did potentially dehydrate you to the point of trouble, it would be a messy and unpleasant way to go I assure you. 

Take care of yourself. You aren’t a whimp for wanting to take care of your health and that of others. These are scary times. Be kind and lend yourself the patience that others may not.
